What we do  ·  Advanced Infrastructure Four contracts. One gap nobody owns.

Residency, recovery, reachability and exit are written as clauses in four separate contracts, and they break in the gaps between them. We assess your estate, meaning all your systems and the providers behind them, as one architecture. You buy the parts directly from whoever you choose.

4–12 WEEKSWRITTEN REQUIREMENTS, NOT A SHORTLISTWE ASSESS · YOU CONTRACT DIRECTLY
Why this pillar exists

Infrastructure is bought in layers and fails across them.

Every organization of scale has a competent network team, a competent storage team and a competent identity team. What it usually does not have is one person who can answer a requirement that touches all three.

01

The requirement has no owner

A residency obligation is written by legal, implemented by storage, and quietly undone by a network re-route. Each team did its job correctly.

02

The supplier assesses against what it supplies

A carrier scopes the requirement against its transport. An integrator against its implementation. Both are competent; neither is neutral.

03

The test is run on the wrong day

Resilience is tested against hardware failure, which almost everything survives, and never against exit, which almost nothing does.

What we assess

Four requirements. Six layers. None of them stays put.

Infrastructure is bought one layer at a time and examined one requirement at a time, and the two never line up. Choose a requirement and watch how far it reaches.

Select a requirement

Six layers of an estate, grouped by what they control: the control plane (who and what is allowed to act), execution and outcome. A requirement is written against one layer and lives in several.

TOUCHEDNOT IN SCOPE

This is why a layer-by-layer purchase produces a requirement with no owner. Each of these was a clause in a separate contract, and the gap between them is where the estate actually fails.

Questions we are asked

Before you ask us.

Who supplies the infrastructure?
A provider you contract directly, under its own licensing. In this pillar Orvix assesses and specifies. Keeping supply separate means we carry no traffic, hold no data and take no margin on what you buy, so our advice has no stake in the purchase.
Which of the three should we start with?
If you can name the layer that worries you, start there: Network as a Service or Storage & Resilience. If the concern is a requirement rather than a layer, or the last two answers you got contradicted each other, start with Infrastructure Design.
Can this run alongside an incumbent integrator?
Yes, and it usually does. We are assessing a requirement, not competing for the implementation. Where an incumbent has done good work, the report says so, and that is a more useful outcome for you than a finding we had to manufacture.

Start with the requirement, not the layer.

Bring the obligation you are least able to evidence. In half an hour we will show you which layers it actually reaches.
